results.note: Read-only documentation-accuracy audit of README.md against the code and the verified-bug catalogs (review/04-exhaustive/VERIFIED-BUGS.md, review/02-findings/catalog.md). I verified the load-bearing claims directly in source where possible. The single most damaging documentation lie is the portability/"it's just Python" promise (README:23,45): the generated standalone Python file is NOT runtime-equivalent to the canvas for optimiser, optimiserApply, modelling, and scenarioExpander nodes — their codegen templates emit `return {first}` pure passthroughs (src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:391-417) and Pipeline.run()/score() execute that literal body with no NODE_REGISTRY dispatch (src/haute/pipeline.py:327-411), so a saved file silently prices DIFFERENTLY than the canvas (catalog findings 1-3, all executed-repro, high). liveSwitch standalone always routes the 'live' branch even under batch (catalog finding 1). Several other marketing claims are overstated against verified behaviour: "prevents the silent crash" (cgroup-blind RAM + silent 4 GiB fallback, finding 31), "test before live" (validate loads a different model than ships, finding 7), "any model, same interface / auto file-change pickup" (stale schema baked into the deployed signature on model swap, finding 8; silent dtype→string serving contract, V048), caching "near-instant / only downstream recalculates" (source-blind column cache + nodeId-only preview slot, findings 35/36), and "see exactly how it was calculated" (trace/explanation evaluator diverges from real Polars, findings 23/27/28/29/47). Git "guardrails" claims (README:140-143) are substantially TRUE in src/haute/_git.py (protected-branch refusal, backup tags, auto-commit before switch) — I did NOT flag them as a lie; the only nuance is that "saves your current work first" is skipped on protected branches by design, which is consistent with the adjacent "protected branches can't be overwritten" claim. Note: the brief's phrase canvas-vs-deploy "prices identically" is NOT a verbatim README string (grep found no "identical"); I have flagged the equivalent implied-equivalence promises the README actually makes ("One pipeline, many uses… No re-exporting", line 163-173, and the portability promise). All line numbers are from the README.md / source as read in this session.

findings.location: README.md:45 ("Why open source matters for pricing")
findings.title: "everything you've built still works - it's just Python" is FALSE for optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander nodes — the standalone file silently prices differently than the canvas
findings.description: The README's central product promise is portability: a pipeline is a standard Python file, and if you stop using Haute "everything you've built still works - it's just Python" (README:45), reinforced by README:23 ("A Python file you can open, read, version, and take with you") and README:81 ("Your file on disk is the source of truth"). This is verifiably broken. The codegen templates for optimiser, optimiserApply, modelling, and scenarioExpander nodes emit a pure passthrough body, while only banding/ratingStep/modelScore emit real apply/score calls. Pipeline.run() and Pipeline.score() execute that literal generated body directly (no exec-side dispatch), so a standalone run of the saved file is a silent no-op for those node types: the optimiser is never applied, the model is never retrained/applied, scenarios never expand. The canvas/executor DOES perform these operations. Result: the saved "it's just Python" file emits un-optimised / wrong prices vs what the user saw in the canvas, with no error.
findings.evidence: README:45 claims "everything you've built still works - it's just Python". Code: src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:391-417 — _SCENARIO_EXPANDER (391-396), _OPTIMISER (398-403), _OPTIMISER_APPLY (405-410), _MODELLING (412-417) all have body `return {first}`. Contrast _MODEL_SCORE:275-284 (`df = score_from_config(...)`), _BANDING_*:337-358 (`apply_banding_from_config`), _RATING_STEP:360-369 (`apply_rating_step_from_config`). src/haute/pipeline.py:327-362 (run) and :364-411 (score) call `n(*input_dfs)` -> Node.__call__ which runs the literal `self.fn` with NO NODE_REGISTRY dispatch. Verified by executed-repro in review/02-findings/catalog.md findings 2 & 3: configured optimiserApply standalone body = `return data_src`, output is value-identical to the raw input (no __optimiser_version__), whereas the executor loads the artifact and applies it.
findings.recommended_fix: Either (a) make the passthrough-body templates emit real config-driven apply calls mirroring modelScore/banding/ratingStep (apply_optimiser_from_config / apply_scenario_expander_from_config / a modelling-apply or load step), so Node.__call__ runs the same logic as the executor; or (b) if some node types are intentionally not standalone-executable, make the generated body raise a loud, explicit error (per CLAUDE.md fail-loud) instead of silently passing through. Until the code is fixed, the README MUST stop claiming unqualified standalone equivalence — qualify the portability promise to the node types that are actually runtime-equivalent, or remove it.

findings.location: README.md:167-173 ("One pipeline, many uses") and README:93 ("Built to be fast")
findings.title: "One pipeline, many uses … No rebuilding, no re-exporting, no maintaining separate versions" overstates canvas/batch/standalone/deploy equivalence that does not hold
findings.description: README:163-173 promises the same pipeline serves Live pricing, Batch scoring, What-if, Impact, and Price-tracing with "No rebuilding, no re-exporting, no maintaining separate versions for different use cases", and README:93 says the batch execution strategy "is chosen automatically - you don't need to configure anything" with the implication it produces the same result as preview. The verified codegen/runtime divergence (see the portability finding) breaks the equivalence between the canvas executor and a standalone batch run (Pipeline.run) for optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander, and for liveSwitch the standalone batch run routes the WRONG input branch. So 'Batch scoring' and 'Live pricing' of the saved file are not guaranteed to match the canvas — exactly the 'maintaining separate versions' problem the README says is eliminated.
findings.evidence: README:171-173 "No rebuilding, no re-exporting, no maintaining separate versions for different use cases." Code paths as in the portability finding (src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:391-417; src/haute/pipeline.py:327-411). liveSwitch: review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 1 (executed-repro): in-canvas executor under source='batch' routes the BATCH frame, the standalone generated body (`return live_src`) routes the LIVE frame — different rows/columns flow downstream silently. _gen_live_switch (src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:268-273,521-539) hard-wires the save-time 'live' input.
findings.recommended_fix: After the codegen fix, this claim becomes true. Until then, soften README:171-173 to state that canvas, deploy, and standalone equivalence holds for the supported node bodies, and explicitly note the node types whose standalone behaviour differs (optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander/liveSwitch).

findings.title: "it prevents the kind of silent crash that can lose work" is overstated — the RAM estimator is cgroup-blind (over-estimates → OOM in containers) and silently falls back to a fixed 4 GiB (under-estimates → silent truncation)
findings.description: README:149-151 claims that before training Haute "probes a sample … to estimate how much memory the full run will need. If it would exceed your machine's available memory, it tells you before you start … This … prevents the kind of silent crash that can lose work." Two verified defects undercut 'prevents': (1) available_ram_bytes reads host /proc/meminfo MemAvailable and ignores cgroup/container memory limits, so on a large node with a small container cgroup it over-estimates usable RAM, decides the dataset fits, and training OOM-kills inside the container — i.e. it does NOT prevent the silent crash it advertises. (2) When detection fails it silently returns a fixed 4 GiB (only a warning log), which on a real large box drives needless aggressive downsampling, training on a silently truncated dataset and deriving prices from it. Either way the outcome is silent, contradicting 'prevents the silent crash'. Separately, the README still says it 'probes a sample of your data', but the implementation was changed to a parquet-metadata approach (no sample probe) per the module docstring — a stale description.
findings.evidence: README:151 "prevents the kind of silent crash that can lose work" and README:149 "probes a sample of your data". Code: src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:1-18 docstring says it REPLACED the probe-based approach with metadata ("This replaces the previous probe-based approach which ran a 1,000-row sample"). available_ram_bytes (src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:51-126) reads /proc/meminfo MemAvailable and has a fixed 4 GiB fallback (only logger.warning('available_ram_fallback_4gib')). review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 31 (executed-repro, medium): fallback returns exactly 4294967296 bytes with no raise; the downsample decision flips False→True purely on the available-RAM value (was_downsampled False@64GiB → True@4GiB, safe_row_limit 626,349 on a 2,000,000-row set); grep found ZERO references to cgroup/memory.max/memory.limit_in_bytes anywhere in src/.
findings.recommended_fix: Tone down README:151 to 'helps avoid' rather than 'prevents', and add the caveat that container/cgroup memory limits are not yet detected (so containerised training can still OOM). Fix README:149 'probes a sample' to reflect the parquet-metadata approach actually implemented. Best: fix available_ram_bytes to honour cgroup limits and fail loudly when RAM is undetectable, then the claim can stand.

findings.location: README.md:123 ("Safe deployments, built in" — "Before anything goes live")
findings.title: "Before anything goes live, Haute runs your pipeline against test inputs" — the test-before-live gate scores a DIFFERENT model than the deployed container ships, and skips the contract check
findings.description: README:123 promises that before deployment Haute runs the pipeline against test inputs and "If anything breaks, the deployment stops", with expected-output tolerances so you test "does it produce the right results." The verified behaviour is that the validate-time gate (score_test_quotes / infer_output_schema) calls score_graph WITHOUT the bundled artifact_paths, so the modelScore intercept never fires: it loads the model live from MLflow (e.g. version='latest', or a since-mutated run artifact) and does NOT run the feature-contract check. At serve time the container passes the pinned bundled artifact and DOES enforce the contract. Net: test quotes can pass while the deployed container produces different prices, and a contract drift that would block serving is invisible to the very gate the README sells as the safety net. This makes 'before anything goes live … if anything breaks, the deployment stops' an overstated guarantee — the gate does not exercise what actually ships.
findings.evidence: README:123. review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 7 (high, executed-repro): src/haute/deploy/_validators.py:375-380 and src/haute/deploy/_schema.py:134-139 call score_graph with no artifact_paths; scorer intercept only engages on remap (src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:605-704), so it falls through to _build_model_score which loads live and skips _assert_runtime_contract_matches. Executed repro: validate path PASSED returning a live-loaded prediction with no contract check; serve path on the IDENTICAL 1-row input raised FeatureMismatchError (contract mismatch). Same input → validation accepts what the deployed container blocks.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the gate to pass resolved.artifacts (the pinned bundle) into score_test_quotes and infer_output_schema so validation routes through the intercept and runs the contract check, identical to serve (the catalog gives the one-line fix). Until then, do not claim the test-before-live gate guarantees the deployed model produces the right results — it tests a potentially different model.

findings.title: "swap a CatBoost model for an XGBoost model without changing your pipeline configuration" + "update a model file and the next run picks it up automatically" — the deploy signature is cached on a fingerprint that ignores model bytes/version, so a model swap ships a stale/wrong serving contract
findings.description: README:109-115 promises model-agnostic swapping with no config change, automatic feature-type casting, and an intelligent cache that watches for file changes so "Update a model file and the next pipeline run picks it up automatically." For the DEPLOY signature path this is verifiably unsafe: infer_output_schema is cached under graph_fingerprint, which hashes only node configs + edge topology + preamble/utility source — NOT model-artifact bytes or the resolved MLflow version. So swapping the underlying model (e.g. regression→classification changing the prediction dtype, or retraining a 'latest'/run artifact in place) leaves the fingerprint byte-identical, the stale cached output schema is reused, and it is baked into the deployed MLflow ModelSignature/manifest. The endpoint then advertises and validates a contract that disagrees with the actual model — the opposite of 'picks it up automatically'. Compounding 'same interface': the serving signature builder silently maps any unrecognised Polars dtype (Decimal/Time/Duration/List/Struct/Binary/etc.) to string (V048), producing a wrong serving contract rather than failing loudly.
findings.evidence: README:113-115. review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 8 (high, executed-repro): graph_fingerprint (src/haute/_cache.py:400-437) excludes model bytes/version; infer_output_schema (src/haute/deploy/_schema.py:95-150) short-circuits on the fingerprint; executed repro shows fingerprint 'byte-identical across model swap: True' and the deployed signature carrying the STALE regression schema ({prediction: Float64}) while the swapped classification model truthfully outputs Int64, with score_graph never re-invoked. V048 (review/04-exhaustive/VERIFIED-BUGS.md): src/haute/deploy/_mlflow.py:239-246 _to_colspecs does dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string), silently stringifying unmapped dtypes.
findings.recommended_fix: Qualify README:115 for the deploy path: the automatic file-change pickup applies to the in-canvas model-load cache, but the deployed serving signature is NOT re-derived on a model-artifact/version change unless config changes (and should be). Fix the fingerprint to include resolved artifact identity, and make _to_colspecs raise on unmapped dtypes (mirroring modelling/_signature.py). Then the 'same interface / auto pickup' claim can stand for deployment.

findings.location: README.md:89-93 ("Built to be fast") — "previewing data at any point is near-instant" / "only the downstream nodes recalculate - everything upstream stays cached"
findings.title: "near-instant" preview and "only downstream recalculates" overstated — node column cache is source-blind (serves stale/wrong columns, needs a manual Refresh) and the preview slot is keyed by nodeId alone (every source/rowLimit toggle forces a full refetch)
findings.description: README:91 claims caching at every node makes previewing "near-instant", and "Change a rating factor and only the downstream nodes recalculate - everything upstream stays cached." Two verified frontend findings qualify this. (1) The preview LRU slot is keyed by nodeId alone while freshness depends on (structuralVersion, source, rowLimit); a node can hold at most one cached preview, so toggling source or rowLimit evicts the other context and forces a full refetch every toggle — not near-instant on the common toggle path (finding 36). (2) Node-level _columns/_availableColumns are source-blind and are not invalidated when the active source changes, so after switching source the cached columns are stale and only a manual Refresh re-previews (finding 35) — i.e. 'stays cached' is true precisely where it is harmful (wrong/stale data), not where it is fast.
findings.evidence: README:91 "previewing data at any point is near-instant" and "everything upstream stays cached". review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 36 (medium, code-trace): preview slot keyed by nodeId alone (one cached preview per node) so source/rowLimit toggles evict and refetch. Finding 35 (medium, code-trace): setActiveSource is a pure state write (frontend useSettingsStore.ts:168), no effect clears node _columns or schedules re-preview, so editors/validators consume the previously-previewed source's schema until a manual Refresh.
findings.recommended_fix: Soften README:91: previews are cached and fast on re-visit of the SAME context, but switching the active source or row limit currently requires a refetch (and a manual Refresh to update node columns). Or fix the cache to be keyed by (nodeId, structuralVersion, source, rowLimit) and invalidate node columns on source change, after which the claim holds.

findings.location: README.md:63-75 ("Click any price. See exactly how it was calculated.")
findings.title: "See exactly how it was calculated" overstated — the trace/explanation evaluator diverges from real Polars for several expression forms, so the displayed lineage can show a value Polars never computed
findings.description: README:63-75 promises that clicking a price traces the path and shows "exactly how it was calculated" at each step, positioned as the answer you give a regulator. Multiple verified findings show the trace/explanation expression evaluator does NOT faithfully reproduce Polars: it silently diverges on replace_strict and other ops (finding 29), returns wrong/None values for horizontal funcs and unsupported functions while displaying them as the computed value (finding 47), the whole parse/evaluate/compute/chain stack wraps everything in `except Exception` and falls back to the raw row value (finding 23, masking evaluator bugs as self-consistent), the positional fast-path attaches the WRONG parent row when a same-row-count transform reorders rows (finding 27), and _fix_upstream_values relocates rows by a 1e-6 absolute tolerance that collides distinct small factors (finding 28). For a feature sold as a regulator-grade explanation, 'exactly how it was calculated' is an over-promise where these paths are exercised.
findings.evidence: README:75 "this gives you that answer in a click" / README:65 "showing the value at each step". review/02-findings/catalog.md finding 29 (medium): expression evaluator silently diverges from Polars on replace_strict. Finding 47 (low): wrong/None for horizontal/unsupported functions, shown as the computed price-explanation value. Finding 23 (medium): except-Exception fallback to raw row value masks evaluator bugs. Finding 27 (medium): positional fast-path attaches wrong parent row on row-reordering transforms. Finding 28 (medium): 1e-6 absolute tolerance collides distinct small-magnitude factors.
findings.recommended_fix: Qualify README:63-75: the trace reflects the pipeline's recorded steps but the per-step value display is a re-evaluation that may diverge from Polars for some expression forms; do not position it as a guaranteed-exact regulator artifact until the evaluator divergences (findings 23/27/28/29/47) are fixed and the silent except-Exception fallback is removed per CLAUDE.md fail-loud.

findings.location: README.md:149 ("Knows your machine's limits") — "probes a sample of your data"
findings.title: README still says the memory estimator "probes a sample of your data" but the implementation was replaced with a parquet-metadata approach (no sample probe)
findings.description: README:149 describes the memory estimate as probing a sample of the data. The implementation explicitly replaced that probe-based approach with a parquet-metadata approach that reads only the file footer (row/column counts), per the module docstring, which calls the old probe 'fragile'. The description is stale — the engine no longer runs a sample through the pipeline to estimate memory.
findings.evidence: README:149 "Haute probes a sample of your data to estimate how much memory the full run will need." src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:1-18 docstring: "Read parquet row-group metadata … This replaces the previous probe-based approach which ran a 1,000-row sample through the pipeline. The probe was fragile … Metadata is always available …".
findings.recommended_fix: Update README:149 to describe the metadata-based estimate (e.g. 'reads your data's parquet metadata to estimate how much memory the full run will need') rather than 'probes a sample'.

results.note: Read-only audit of user-facing guides under docs/ (getting-started, building-models, deployment, deployment/ci, deployment/targets) cross-checked against src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py, src/haute/_scaffold.py, src/haute/cli/_serve.py, src/haute/deploy/_mlflow.py, src/haute/executor.py and the generated-scaffold reality. The most damaging defects are the ones where following a guide verbatim produces a BROKEN deploy or a project layout that does not exist. The single highest-impact issue: every deployment guide tells users to configure Databricks CI secrets named DATABRICKS_HOST/DATABRICKS_TOKEN, but the scaffolded CI workflow and the deploy code consume DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST/DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN, so a by-the-book setup fails its first production deploy. Equally pervasive: the docs claim the pipeline lives at root main.py with pipeline = "main.py", while haute init actually DELETES the uv-init root main.py and scaffolds rating/main.py with pipeline = "rating/main.py". No files modified.

findings.title: Every deploy guide names Databricks CI secrets DATABRICKS_HOST/DATABRICKS_TOKEN, but the generated CI workflow and deploy code require DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST/DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN — a by-the-book setup fails its first deploy
findings.description: All four user-facing deployment guides instruct the reader to add CI secrets named exactly DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN (presented as 'the two values you need'). The CI deploy job that consumes them does not read those names. src/haute/_scaffold.py defines the databricks target's `secrets` list as ["DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST", "DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN"] (lines 33-36), so the generated deploy-staging.yml env: block only injects DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST/DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN. The deploy path reads the same RATING names and hard-fails if absent.
findings.evidence: Docs (databricks.md Step 3): 'The two values you need are: DATABRICKS_HOST | Your workspace URL ; DATABRICKS_TOKEN | Your personal access token'. Code: src/haute/_scaffold.py:33-36 secrets=["DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST","DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN"]; src/haute/deploy/_mlflow.py:375-380 `host = os.environ.get("DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST", "")` ... raises 'DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST is not set. Add it to .env or set it as a CI secret.' The project's own design note docs/MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_STANDARDISATION.md:40 confirms 'deploy uses different env vars (DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST/TOKEN)'. A user who sets only DATABRICKS_HOST/DATABRICKS_TOKEN as CI secrets (exactly as the guides say) will have the staging/production deploy job fail the credential check.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the secret-name tables in databricks.md (Step 3 + checklist line 371), github-actions.md (lines 117-118), gitlab.md (lines 112-113), azure-devops.md (lines 113-114) and deployment/index.md to list DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST and DATABRICKS_RATING_TOKEN as the secrets the deploy job actually consumes (the .env.example the scaffold writes lists both pairs, with the RATING pair labelled 'Production serving endpoint credentials'). State clearly which pair the CD job uses. Better still, reconcile naming between scaffold/docs so there is one canonical pair.

findings.title: Docs say the pipeline is root `main.py` with `pipeline = "main.py"`; the scaffold deletes root main.py and writes `rating/main.py` with `pipeline = "rating/main.py"`
findings.description: Every haute.toml sample in the guides sets `pipeline = "main.py"` and the surrounding prose treats `main.py` as a project-root file. The generated haute.toml hardcodes `pipeline = "rating/main.py"`, and the starter pipeline is written to rating/main.py. Worse, haute init explicitly removes any root main.py left by `uv init`. A user editing root main.py (as the docs imply) would be editing a deleted/non-existent file, and a hand-written `pipeline = "main.py"` would not resolve.
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/_scaffold.py:227 `pipeline = "rating/main.py"`; src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:383-386 'Remove root main.py left over from `uv init`' -> root_main.unlink(); :400 writes rating/main.py. Docs: deployment/index.md:85 and databricks.md:203 and docker.md:72 all show `pipeline = "main.py"`; before-you-start.md:125 lists '`main.py` | Your pricing pipeline' as a root file.
findings.recommended_fix: Change every `pipeline = "main.py"` to `pipeline = "rating/main.py"`, and update prose/file-listing tables to refer to rating/main.py (with rating/utility/, rating/config/). Note that haute init deletes the uv-init root main.py so readers don't go looking for it.

findings.title: The `haute init` before/after directory tree is fabricated: it shows root main.py persisting unchanged and claims 'nothing is overwritten', but init deletes root main.py and scaffolds a rating/ tree
findings.description: The before/after illustration shows `main.py` at the project root in BOTH columns (unchanged by init) and the caption asserts 'Nothing is overwritten - haute init only adds new files'. In reality haute init (1) deletes the root main.py created by `uv init`, (2) creates a whole rating/ subtree (rating/main.py, rating/__init__.py, rating/utility/, rating/config/data_source/raw_rows.json, rating/config/quote_response/priced.json, rating/models/, rating/outputs/), plus data/, prompts/, .githooks/, and tests/test_pipeline.py — none of which appear in the 'after' tree. It also APPENDS to .gitignore (mutating an existing file) and adds data/ to .gitignore.
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:384-386 deletes root main.py; :388-416 builds rating/* tree; :380-381 creates data/ and prompts/; :436-439 writes tests/test_pipeline.py; :496-505 appends a '# Haute' block to existing .gitignore; :497 gitignore entries include 'data/'. Docs tree (deployment/index.md:60-72) shows only haute.toml, .env.example, .gitignore, tests/quotes/, .github/workflows/ added and main.py kept at root.
findings.recommended_fix: Redraw the after-tree to reflect the real layout (rating/main.py + rating/utility/ + rating/config/, data/, prompts/, tests/test_pipeline.py, tests/quotes/, .githooks/pre-commit, .env.example, ci files). Replace 'Nothing is overwritten' with the accurate behaviour: the uv-init root main.py is removed, and an existing .gitignore is appended to (not replaced).

findings.title: github-actions.md calls the generated merge-to-main workflow `deploy.yml`; the scaffold actually writes `deploy-staging.yml`
findings.description: The guide repeatedly names the middle of the three GitHub workflow files `deploy.yml` (in the summary table, the ?? reference block, and the troubleshooting section). The scaffold writes the file as deploy-staging.yml. A user following the doc to find/edit `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` will not find it. (gitlab.md and azure-devops.md name their single files correctly; only the GitHub guide is wrong.)
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:447-458 writes '.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml' and lists ci_files = [ci.yml, deploy-staging.yml, deploy-production.yml]. Docs: github-actions.md:29 '| `deploy.yml` | When you merge to main |', :204 '`deploy.yml` - Merge to main', :266 'Make sure the `deploy.yml` paths filter matches'. The generated file's internal `name:` is 'Deploy' (src/haute/_scaffold.py:414), which may be the source of the confusion, but the filename is deploy-staging.yml.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace `deploy.yml` with `deploy-staging.yml` throughout github-actions.md (table row, reference block heading, troubleshooting). Optionally clarify that the workflow's display name is 'Deploy' while its filename is deploy-staging.yml.

findings.title: github-actions.md documents the deploy paths filter as `"*.py"`; the generated workflow filters on `"rating/**"`, so the documented filter would never match the actual pipeline file
findings.description: The reference YAML for the deploy workflow lists the push paths filter as `"*.py"`, `"haute.toml"`, `"data/**"`, `"models/**"`, `"tests/quotes/**"`. The real generated workflow uses `"rating/**"` instead of `"*.py"` (and has no top-level *.py files since the pipeline now lives under rating/). This matters because the same guide's troubleshooting (line 266) tells users the paths filter governs whether a deploy triggers; a user reasoning from the documented `*.py` filter would wrongly conclude an edit to rating/main.py won't deploy (it does) or that a root .py change will deploy (there is none).
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/_scaffold.py:419-424 paths: - "rating/**" - "haute.toml" - "data/**" - "models/**" - "tests/quotes/**" (note: no "*.py", and a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger is also present). Docs: github-actions.md:212-217 shows paths: - "*.py" - "haute.toml" - "data/**" - "models/**" - "tests/quotes/**".
findings.recommended_fix: Update the documented paths list to match the generated file: replace `"*.py"` with `"rating/**"` and mention the additional `workflow_dispatch` trigger. Align the troubleshooting bullet accordingly.

findings.title: docker.md shows base_image = "python:3.11-slim"; the scaffold generates "python:3.11.9-slim"
findings.description: The Docker target guide's haute.toml example and the per-setting table both show base_image = "python:3.11-slim". The scaffold-generated [deploy.container] block pins the patch version: base_image = "python:3.11.9-slim". Minor, but it means the documented config does not byte-match what haute init produces, and a reader copying the doc's value silently changes the pinned base image.
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/_scaffold.py:63 (and :90, :118, :146) base_image = "python:3.11.9-slim". Docs: docker.md:82 base_image = "python:3.11-slim" and :96 '| `base_image` | The base Docker image to build from | `"python:3.11-slim"` |'.
findings.recommended_fix: Change both occurrences in docker.md to "python:3.11.9-slim" to match the generated default (or, if the doc intends to show the non-pinned form, note that the scaffold pins the patch version).

findings.title: polars.md claims utility helpers are 'available in every code node without needing to import them'; helpers are only in scope via an explicit `from utility.features import ...` in the pipeline preamble
findings.description: polars.md states: 'Your project's utility/ folder contains helper functions that are available in every code node without needing to import them.' Code-node execution resolves names from the pipeline file's preamble (the import/definition block extracted from the .py file), with the project root inserted on sys.path so `from utility.features import clean_columns` resolves. There is no evidence of blanket auto-injection of utility symbols into every node namespace; the companion guide preparing-your-data.md:82 itself shows the explicit `from utility.features import clean_columns, to_date, years_between`. So the 'no import needed' promise overstates reality and can confuse a user who writes clean_columns() in a node without an import present in the file.
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/executor.py:421-424 'Ensure project root is importable so `from utility.xxx import …` works' and inserts cwd + pipeline parent dir; _ast_helpers.py:462-508 _extract_preamble pulls user import/definition lines from the file; preamble_imports_utility gates utility-module eviction (executor.py:368). The starter rating/main.py (src/haute/_scaffold.py:957-1002) does NOT import the utilities, yet features.py's docstring says 'These are imported into main.py'. Docs contradiction: polars.md:90 'without needing to import them' vs preparing-your-data.md:82 explicit import.
findings.recommended_fix: Soften polars.md to: helpers in rating/utility/ are importable from your pipeline (e.g. `from utility.features import clean_columns`) and, once imported in the file's preamble, are available to your code nodes. Align with preparing-your-data.md which shows the explicit import. Also fix the path reference (utility/ actually lives at rating/utility/).

findings.title: installing-haute.md describes what `haute init` creates without mentioning it removes the root main.py and scaffolds a rating/ pipeline tree
findings.description: The page says haute init 'creates a new project folder with everything Haute needs: a haute.toml configuration file, test quote templates, CI/CD workflow files, and a .env.example credential template.' This omits the load-bearing facts that init deletes the uv-init root main.py and that the actual pipeline + utilities + config sidecars are scaffolded under rating/. A first-time user who runs `uv init my-pricing-project` then `haute init` will see their root main.py disappear with no warning in this guide.
findings.evidence: Code: src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:383-386 removes root main.py; :388-416 scaffolds rating/main.py + rating/utility/ + rating/config/*. The CLI's own summary (src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:516-520) does print 'rating/' and 'rating/utility/', so the running command is honest; only the doc omits it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a sentence noting that haute init replaces the uv-init root main.py with a starter pipeline at rating/main.py and scaffolds rating/utility/ and rating/config/ alongside data/, prompts/, and tests/.

results.note: Read-only audit. Each finding cross-checked against implementation, not just doc-vs-doc. Reference: review/04-exhaustive/candidates.json:4303 independently flags the quasibinomial dead entry; this audit additionally identifies the upstream DESIGN-DOC claims that assert those families are supported. Planning/*.md docs are mostly honestly status-labelled ("working plan", "implemented in the current branch"); the drift concentrates in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md. Cache sizes (16/8) and the 14-folder config map in ARCHITECTURE.md were checked and are ACCURATE — not reported.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE claims "17 node types" but the implementation has 20 (edgeJoin and explore are omitted entirely)
findings.description: The architecture document repeatedly states there are exactly 17 node types, enumerates 17 in its tables, and asserts "All 17 types are defined in _types.py" and that nodeTypes.ts holds "defaults for all 17 types". The actual NodeType(StrEnum) in src/haute/_types.py:25-49 defines 20 members. Two of them are fully-built, registered, user-relevant node types the doc never mentions: EDGE_JOIN = "edgeJoin" and EXPLORE = "explore". This misleads a reader about the product surface (an entire join node and an explore/EDA node are invisible in the canonical architecture reference) and makes the node-type tables an unreliable index.
findings.evidence: Doc: "There are 17 node types grouped by function" (ARCHITECTURE.md:49); "All 17 types are defined in `_types.py`" (:93); "NODE_TYPE_META: icons, colours, labels, defaults for all 17 types" (:544). Code: src/haute/_types.py:32-49 lists 20 enum members including `EDGE_JOIN = "edgeJoin"` (:35) and `EXPLORE = "explore"` (:41). EDGE_JOIN is implemented (planning/EDGE_JOIN_NODE_SPEC.md: "Status: implemented in the current branch for v1"); EXPLORE has a registered builder `_build_explore` with a column contract (src/haute/_builders.py:676-701) and a service module (referenced by VERIFIED-BUGS V099 _explore_service.py). Neither appears in any ARCHITECTURE.md node table.
findings.recommended_fix: Update §3.2 to the real count and add Explore (EDA/profiling) and Edge Join (insert a join onto an existing edge) to the node-type tables; correct the three '17' references (:49, :93, :544). Consider a test that asserts the documented node count equals len(NodeType) to prevent recurrence.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE states all rating tables live in Databricks Unity Catalog, but rating tables are stored as in-repo JSON sidecars and executed from inline entries
findings.description: §8.3 is a 'Finalised' design decision asserting that ALL rating tables (even small ones) live in Databricks Unity Catalog, are referenced by a catalog.schema.table URI, and that this 'avoids CSV sprawl in git'. The shipped rating-step subsystem does the opposite: rating table values are stored inline in JSON sidecars under config/rating_step/<name>.json (version-controlled in git) and the executor builds the lookup directly from those inline entries via pl.DataFrame(entries). No catalog.schema.table URI, no Unity Catalog dependency. This misleads users about where load-bearing pricing data lives and how it is governed/edited (a correctness-relevant claim for an insurance pricing engine).
findings.evidence: Doc: "All rating tables (even small ones) live in Databricks Unity Catalog. Referenced by `catalog.schema.table` URI ... keeps a single source of truth and avoids CSV sprawl in git." (ARCHITECTURE.md:794-795). Contradicted by docs/RATING_STEP_DESIGN.md (entries stored in config/rating_step/ JSON sidecars, expanded on load) and docs/CONFIG_SIDECAR_DESIGN.md:111-183. Code: src/haute/_rating.py:512-540 reads `entries` from config and constructs `lookup = pl.DataFrame(entries)`; grep for 'catalog'/'unity'/'databricks' in _rating.py returns no rating-table-source usage.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite §8.3 to describe the actual design: rating tables are stored as JSON sidecars in config/rating_step/ (git-versioned, GUI-editable), built into Polars lookups from inline entries at execution time. If Databricks-sourced rating tables remain a future goal, mark it explicitly as planned rather than 'Finalised'.

findings.location: docs/GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md:120 (§3.3 Supported Families table); also §5.3 mockup :586
findings.title: GLM design lists a "quasibinomial" family that no surface offers or supports (the focus-example drift)
findings.description: The GLM design doc's 'Supported Families' table lists `quasibinomial` (logit, 'Overdispersed binary') as a supported family. It is offered by no surface and accepted by no code path: the frontend family picker omits it, the backend family/link validator rejects it, and the RustyStats fit layer never special-cases it. The only trace of 'quasibinomial' anywhere in the product is a dead key in the frontend CANONICAL_LINKS map (which is unreachable because the FAMILIES list it keys off never contains that value). An analyst reading the design would believe quasibinomial GLMs are trainable; they are not.
findings.evidence: Doc: GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md:120 table row `| quasibinomial | logit | Overdispersed binary |`. Frontend: FAMILIES in frontend/src/panels/modelling/GLMTargetConfig.tsx:7-15 lists only poisson, gamma, tweedie, gaussian, binomial, quasipoisson, negbinomial (no quasibinomial); the only quasibinomial reference is the unreachable CANONICAL_LINKS entry at :24. Backend: _VALID_GLM_LINKS in src/haute/routes/_train_service.py:118-125 has no quasibinomial, and _validate_glm_family_link (:128-148, called on the live train path at :668) raises HTTP 400 for any unknown family. Independently flagged as a dead entry in review/04-exhaustive/candidates.json:4303.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the `quasibinomial` row from the §3.3 Supported Families table (and the §5.3 mockup if shown). Separately, the unreachable CANONICAL_LINKS['quasibinomial'] in GLMTargetConfig.tsx:24 should be deleted, but that is a code cleanup, not part of the doc fix.

findings.title: GLM design's family list diverges from the backend validator: it lists negbinomial/quasipoisson as supported (they are rejected) and omits inverse_gaussian (which is supported)
findings.description: Beyond quasibinomial, the §3.3 Supported Families table is out of sync with the authoritative backend validator in two more ways. (1) It lists `quasipoisson` and `negbinomial` as supported families, but the live training validator _validate_glm_family_link only accepts {gaussian, binomial, poisson, gamma, tweedie, inverse_gaussian}; submitting quasipoisson or negbinomial returns HTTP 400 — even though the frontend FAMILIES picker offers both, so a user who follows the UI hits a backend rejection. (2) The table omits `inverse_gaussian`, which the backend DOES support with four links. The doc is thus simultaneously over-promising (two families that don't work) and under-documenting (one family that does).
findings.evidence: Doc supported families (GLM_INTEGRATION_DESIGN.md:114-121): gaussian, poisson, gamma, tweedie, binomial, quasipoisson, negbinomial, quasibinomial. Backend truth (src/haute/routes/_train_service.py:118-125): _VALID_GLM_LINKS keys = gaussian, binomial, poisson, gamma, tweedie, inverse_gaussian; _validate_glm_family_link (:132-136) raises 400 for anything else. Frontend FAMILIES (GLMTargetConfig.tsx:7-15) offers quasipoisson + negbinomial. RustyStats fit (src/haute/modelling/_rustystats.py:112-143) passes `family` straight through and only special-cases 'tweedie', so it adds no extra family validation.
findings.recommended_fix: Reconcile §3.3 with _VALID_GLM_LINKS: either (a) make it the documented superset and clearly mark which families are actually wired end-to-end, or (b) trim it to exactly {gaussian, binomial, poisson, gamma, tweedie, inverse_gaussian} and add inverse_gaussian. Note the separate code bug (UI offers quasipoisson/negbinomial that the backend rejects) for the engineering backlog.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE documents a `haute.testing.PipelineTestCase` API and `haute test` command that do not exist
findings.description: §6.3 presents a concrete, copy-pasteable code example importing `from haute.testing import PipelineTestCase` with methods assert_pipeline_valid / assert_has_output / sample_record, and §6.1 lists 'haute test runs them' as a baked-in practice. Neither exists: there is no haute.testing module / PipelineTestCase symbol anywhere in the source, and the CLI registers no `test` command. A user copying the §6.3 example gets an ImportError. (§10 Phase 5 does mark 'Auto-generated test stubs + haute test' as unchecked, but §6 presents the API as a delivered feature with no caveat — the two sections contradict each other.)
findings.evidence: Doc: ARCHITECTURE.md:728 `from haute.testing import PipelineTestCase`; :710 '`pytest` stubs auto-generated for each pipeline; `haute test` runs them'. Code: grep for 'PipelineTestCase'/'assert_pipeline_valid'/'haute.testing' across the repo matches ONLY ARCHITECTURE.md (no source). CLI command registration (src/haute/cli/__init__.py:22-30) is exactly: deploy, impact, init, lint, run, serve, smoke, status, train — no `test`. Phase 5 (:974) lists '[ ] Auto-generated test stubs + haute test' as not done.
findings.recommended_fix: Either remove the §6.3 PipelineTestCase example and the §6.1 'haute test' row, or clearly label them as planned/not-yet-implemented and replace the import example with a note that the testing harness is forthcoming. Align §6 with the Phase-5 unchecked status.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE presents `haute diff HEAD~1` as a feature, but no diff command exists
findings.description: §9.5 'Pipeline Visual Diff (the engineering team feature)' shows `haute diff HEAD~1` and describes a working side-by-side graph diff with green/red/amber nodes. The CLI has no `diff` command and there is no diff command module. §10 Phase 5 does list it as unchecked, but §9 'Killer Features' frames it in present tense alongside shipped features with no 'planned' marker, so a reader skimming the feature list would reasonably assume it works.
findings.evidence: Doc: ARCHITECTURE.md:885 '`haute diff HEAD~1`' under '### 9.5 Pipeline Visual Diff (the engineering team feature)'. Code: src/haute/cli/__init__.py registers no diff command; no _diff.py in src/haute/cli/ (cli dir contains _deploy/_impact/_init_cmd/_lint/_run/_serve/_smoke/_status/_train/_helpers). Phase 5 (:975) '[ ] Pipeline visual diff (`haute diff HEAD~1`)'.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit 'Planned' / 'Not yet implemented' marker to §9.5 (the section header or a leading sentence), consistent with the Phase-5 checkbox, so the killer-features list doesn't imply it ships today.

findings.title: DEPLOY_DESIGN documents `haute rollback` with usage examples, but the command is unimplemented (Phase P8 'Planned')
findings.description: §7.4 'Rollback' shows two concrete invocations (`haute rollback motor-pricing`, `haute rollback motor-pricing --to 3`) and describes Databricks/container rollback behaviour as if available. There is no rollback command in the CLI. The same document's own status table §9 lists 'P8 — haute rollback command — Planned', so §7.4 over-states current capability relative to §9. For a safety-critical deploy doc, presenting an unbuilt rollback path as usable is materially misleading.
findings.evidence: Doc: DEPLOY_DESIGN.md:464-469 fenced bash block `haute rollback motor-pricing` / `--to 3`, plus 'Databricks: updates serving endpoint to previous model version. Container: re-tags previous image and redeploys.' Code: src/haute/cli/__init__.py:22-30 registers no rollback; no _rollback.py module. Same doc §9:509 '| **P8** | `haute rollback` command | Planned |'.
findings.recommended_fix: Prefix §7.4 with a 'Planned (P8)' marker and either remove the example invocations or mark them as the intended future interface, so §7.4 and the §9 status table agree.

findings.location: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:654 (§5.3 Deploy Targets table, Container row 'Status: Next')
findings.title: ARCHITECTURE marks the Container deploy target as 'Next' (not built), but it is implemented and dispatched in code (and DEPLOY_DESIGN says 'Implemented')

Contradicted by DEPLOY_DESIGN.md:89 '| **Container** | `"container"` | Docker image (FastAPI) | None (local/manual) | ✅ Implemented |'. Code: src/haute/deploy/__init__.py:75-78 `if target == "container": from haute.deploy._container import deploy_to_container; return deploy_to_container(resolved)`; deploy_to_container defined at src/haute/deploy/_container.py:170 (with a NotImplementedError only for the platform service-update step at :230).

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE's deploy-target list omits the azure-container-apps / aws-ecs / gcp-run targets that the init CLI actually offers

findings.evidence: Doc: ARCHITECTURE.md:25 'Databricks, container, SageMaker, Azure ML'; :203 'databricks, container, sagemaker, azure-ml'; §5.3 table (:653-657) lists only those four. Code: src/haute/cli/_init_cmd.py:535-545 click.Choice = ['databricks','container','azure-container-apps','aws-ecs','gcp-run','sagemaker','azure-ml']. DEPLOY_DESIGN.md:86-94 documents all seven.

findings.location: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:105 (§3.3 "14 of the 17 node types store external config")
findings.title: ARCHITECTURE's "14 of the 17 node types store external config" framing is stale (there are 20 node types; the 14-folder map and folder list are otherwise correct)
findings.description: §3.3 says '14 of the 17 node types store external config (all except polars, submodel, and submodelPort)'. The count of config-bearing types (14) and the listed folders are accurate against NODE_TYPE_TO_FOLDER, but the denominator '17' is wrong (the enum has 20) and the 'all except polars/submodel/submodelPort' exclusion is incomplete — explore and edgeJoin are also config-folderless. Same root cause as the '17 node types' finding; minor on its own but compounds the stale node inventory.
findings.evidence: Doc: ARCHITECTURE.md:105 '14 of the 17 node types store external config (all except `polars`, `submodel`, and `submodelPort`)'. Code: NODE_TYPE_TO_FOLDER (src/haute/_config_io.py:41-56) has exactly 14 entries (matching the doc's folder table), but NodeType has 20 members (_types.py:32-49); types WITHOUT a config folder are polars, submodel, submodelPort, explore, AND edgeJoin (5, not 3).

results.note: Scope: public-API docstrings in src/haute/{pipeline,__init__,parser,codegen,schemas,executor}.py — the bodies mkdocstrings is configured to render (mkdocs.yml:83-89, handler python, paths:[src], show_source/show_root_heading). IMPORTANT RENDERING CAVEAT: although mkdocstrings is enabled, the docs nav (mkdocs.yml:91-140) contains NO API-reference page and there are zero `::: haute.*` autodoc directives anywhere under docs/, so in the CURRENT site build none of these docstrings are actually rendered to a page. They are, however, the public-API docstrings shown in IDEs/help() and would render verbatim the moment any `::: haute.pipeline` block is added (which the config invites). I therefore audited them as the public API surface and weighted severity with this caveat. Verification: I ran the Pipeline and Submodel docstring usage examples and a score()-seeding probe against the real package in .venv (scratch scripts under a temp dir, since deleted; no audited file modified). Cross-checked claims against review/02-findings/catalog.md (findings #6, #9) and the VERIFIED-BUGS sweep. The Pipeline class example (pipeline.py:270-281) runs cleanly; score()'s "all sources are seeded" claim is accurate (both sources received the seed df). The findings below are docstrings that mislead about behaviour/correctness, ordered by product impact.

findings.title: Submodel docstring usage example does not run — connect() references an undefined node 'policies' and raises ValueError
findings.description: The `Submodel` class docstring's `Usage::` example registers exactly ONE node (`frequency_model`, via `@submodel.external_file`, whose parameter happens to be named `policies`) and then calls `submodel.connect("policies", "frequency_model")`. `"policies"` is a function PARAMETER name, not a registered node — no node named `policies` exists. `NodeRegistry.connect` (pipeline.py:235-238) validates the source node against `self._node_map` and raises `ValueError`. So the single illustrative example for how to build a Submodel crashes if a user copies it. Real submodel files (e.g. modules/submodel.py:17-53) always register the upstream source node (`@submodel.data_source(...) def policies(...)`) BEFORE connecting it, which is the missing line here.
findings.evidence: Executed the example verbatim against the installed package: `sm = haute.Submodel('model_scoring'); @sm.external_file(path='models/freq.cbm', file_type='catboost') def frequency_model(policies): ...; sm.connect('policies','frequency_model')` -> `ValueError: Source node 'policies' not found in pipeline. Known nodes: ['frequency_model']` (raised at pipeline.py:236). The contrasting Pipeline class example (pipeline.py:270-281) runs to completion. Grep confirms every real submodel file defines the source node before connecting (modules/submodel.py:17 `@submodel.data_source(...) def policy_data`, then connect; modules/fttgggg.py similarly).
findings.recommended_fix: Make the example self-consistent like real submodel files: add a source node before connecting, e.g. add `@submodel.data_source(config="config/data_source/policies.json")\n        def policies(): ...` above `frequency_model`, OR rename the connect endpoints so they reference nodes that actually exist (e.g. connect frequency_model to a downstream node that is also defined). Verify the corrected snippet executes.

findings.location: src/haute/codegen.py:76-84 (`_format_contract_kwarg` docstring) vs codegen.py:106-113 (`except Exception` body)
findings.title: Docstring frames the opaque-contract rescue as 'infrastructure failures' only, but the code downgrades ANY non-ConfigError (TypeError/KeyError/ContractMismatchError) to contract="opaque"
findings.description: The docstring says: contract computation 'loads an MLflow artifact ... that load can fail in disconnected environments or CI runs. We treat *infrastructure* failures (MLflow unreachable, artifact missing) as "opaque at codegen time"'. This tells a reader the rescue is scoped to environmental/infra errors and that real bugs would surface. The implementation catches `except ConfigError: raise` then `except Exception:` -> returns `contract="opaque"` (with only a warning) for EVERY other exception type, including genuine code defects (TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError) and contract-integrity errors (ContractMismatchError, which is a HauteError, not a ConfigError). VERIFIED bug catalog #9 reproduces this: a malformed banding `factors=["age"]` makes the real `_banding_columns` raise AttributeError, which is silently emitted as `contract="opaque"`. The docstring thus misrepresents the rescue's breadth and hides that it violates the repo's fail-loud mandate for non-infra errors.
findings.evidence: Docstring (codegen.py:79-82): 'We treat *infrastructure* failures (MLflow unreachable, artifact missing) as "opaque at codegen time"'. Code (codegen.py:106-113): `except Exception as exc: logger.warning('contract_emit_opaque_on_error', ...); return f'contract="{OPAQUE_CONTRACT_SENTINEL}"'` — no exception-type narrowing; ContractMismatchError (errors.py, subclass of HauteError not ConfigError) and TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError all hit this arm. catalog.md finding #9 (executed-repro, exit 0): TypeError, ContractMismatchError, and a real unpatched AttributeError from `_banding_columns` on a malformed factor are each downgraded to contract="opaque" with only a warning; only ConfigError propagates.
findings.recommended_fix: Either (a) narrow the docstring to state plainly that the rescue catches all non-ConfigError exceptions and downgrades them to an opaque contract (documenting the actual, broad behaviour), or preferably (b) fix the code to also re-raise HauteError (covering ContractMismatchError) and let TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError propagate, then the docstring's 'infrastructure failures' framing becomes truthful. Whichever path, doc and code must agree.

findings.title: parse_pipeline_file docstring promises 'valid nodes are returned alongside broken ones' on syntax errors, but the regex fallback silently drops ALL submodels and their nodes/edges
findings.description: The docstring states: 'On syntax errors the file is still parsed via regex fallback so that valid nodes are returned alongside broken ones.' This implies the fallback preserves the user's valid structure. VERIFIED catalog finding #6 (high, executed-repro) shows the regex fallback path (`_parser_regex.fallback_parse`) contains zero submodel handling: when a pipeline references `pipeline.submodel('modules/sub.py')` and the main file has any syntax error, every submodel child node and edge is silently discarded and `submodels` is None — even though those submodel files are independently valid. Under the GUI default (flatten=False) the submodel placeholder node disappears; a subsequent save persists the truncated graph, permanently deleting submodel wiring. Submodel child nodes ARE 'valid nodes', so the docstring's blanket 'valid nodes are returned' overstates completeness and hides a data-loss path.
findings.evidence: Docstring: parser.py:87-88 '...still parsed via regex fallback so that valid nodes are returned alongside broken ones.' parse_pipeline_source catches SyntaxError and `return _fallback_parse(...)` (parser.py:145-147), short-circuiting BEFORE the submodel block at parser.py:181-211 that the healthy path runs. catalog.md #6 repro `parser__regex-fallback-drops-all-submodels.py` (PASS): broken main.py + valid modules/sub.py -> fallback graph node ids ['root_node'] only (submodel child 'child_node' / placeholder 'submodel__unnamed' dropped), submodels=None; only a generic 'syntax errors' warning shown.
findings.recommended_fix: Tighten the docstring to scope the promise to MAIN-FILE decorated nodes and explicitly warn that submodels referenced via pipeline.submodel() are NOT recovered by the regex fallback (and may be lost on save). Better, also reference the intended remediation (recover submodel calls in the fallback) once implemented, and keep the docstring honest in the interim so callers do not assume completeness.

findings.title: execute_graph Returns block documents a plain 5-key dict, but the function returns dict[str, NodeResult] (a ~15-field Pydantic model)
findings.description: The `Returns:` block documents the value as `Dict mapping node_id -> { "status": ..., "row_count": int, "columns": [...], "preview": [...], "error": str | None }` — i.e. a bare dict with five keys. The actual return type (and signature annotation) is `dict[str, NodeResult]`, where `NodeResult` (schemas.py:229-244) is a Pydantic model with ~15 fields (column_count, available_columns, preview_columns, preview_row_count, preview_row_limit, preview_truncated, error_line, timing_ms, memory_bytes, schema_warnings, ...). A consumer following the docstring would treat results as plain dicts (`r["status"]`) rather than attribute access on a model (`r.status`), and would be unaware of the richer fields they can rely on. Minor because the true type is in the signature annotation, but the prose contradicts it.
findings.evidence: Docstring Returns (executor.py:847-855) shows the literal dict with keys status/row_count/columns/preview/error. Signature: `def execute_graph(...) -> dict[str, NodeResult]:` (executor.py:805-817). Construction sites build `NodeResult(...)` Pydantic objects (executor.py:1167, 1189, 1199, 1227). results.note: Read-only documentation-accuracy audit of in-code comments in the six target files, cross-checked against the code they describe and against review/04-exhaustive/VERIFIED-BUGS.md (V015, V016, V035) and review/02-findings/catalog.md. No files modified. Two findings are high-confidence comment lies that mislead about CORRECTNESS (one verified by the exhaustive sweep, one a direct self-contradiction with the cached_property that backs it). Comments that I checked and judged ACCURATE (not flagged): _json_shred.py:514-520 _resolve_leaf list-collapse note (honestly calls itself 'degenerate'); _optimiser_service.py:1296 gini cross-reference (verified _gini does return 0.0 for single-row input); _cache.py:202-211 edge-serialization comment (its claims are scoped to edges and are correct for edges — the V035 non-injectivity bug is in the unframed NODE line at :200 and the extra_keys join at :431, which this comment does not cover, so the comment itself does not lie); _trace_enrichment.py module docstring and detect_row_lineage_type docstring (match code).

findings.title: Header comment asserts a JSON key 'can't be $value ... so there's no collision' — false, and the collision silently drops every row of an affected table
findings.description: The module header comment states that the reserved leaf token `$value` (`_SCALAR_VALUE_LEAF`) for scalar-array child tables is safe because 'a JSON key can't be `$value` in this path grammar, so there's no collision with a real field.' This invariant claim is false. `parse_column_path` (src/haute/_api_input_schema.py:224-242) returns the column's leaf verbatim with no escaping or guarding, and `validate_v2_schema` does not reject a real `$value` key on an object table. So a record carrying a real key named `"$value"` produces an object-table column whose leaf equals `_SCALAR_VALUE_LEAF`; at shred time `_walk`'s `is_scalar_table` test (lines 628-630) then misclassifies the object table as a scalar table and the shape check drops EVERY record of that table. This is VERIFIED bug V015 in review/04-exhaustive/VERIFIED-BUGS.md (executed repro V015.py). The comment is the load-bearing justification for the whole `$value` sentinel design, so it actively misleads any reader/reviewer into believing the collision is impossible.
findings.evidence: Comment (lines 70-71): "a reserved ``$value`` leaf meaning \"the element itself\" (a JSON key can't be ``$value`` in this path grammar, so there's no collision with a real field)."  Actual: parse_column_path returns the raw tail leaf unmodified; validate_v2_schema has no guard rejecting leaf == '$value' on a non-scalar table. VERIFIED-BUGS V015: "That assertion is false ... shred_to_buffers silently drops EVERY record of that table." The related V016 shows the same unescaped `f"{table_path}.{col_name}"` path construction also breaks on keys containing a literal dot.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the comment to state plainly that a literal `$value` key (or a key containing a dot) IS expressible and WOULD collide, and that the collision is/should be rejected at validation time. Then back the comment with a real guard in validate_v2_schema (raise ApiInputSchemaError when a column leaf equals `_SCALAR_VALUE_LEAF` and the table is not a pure scalar-array child table), so the comment and the code agree and the failure is loud rather than silent (matches the project's fail-loud rule). Do not leave the false 'no collision' assertion in place.

findings.title: _graph_base_fingerprint docstring says it is 'Always recomputed ... when the graph instance is mutated' — but it is memoized once per instance via a cached_property, and the public path reads the cached value
findings.description: The `_graph_base_fingerprint` docstring claims the base fingerprint is 'Always recomputed to avoid serving stale cached results when the graph instance is mutated (e.g. node config changes).' This describes behaviour that no longer exists. The public entry point `graph_fingerprint` (lines 423/435) reads `graph._haute_base_fingerprint`, which is a `@cached_property` on PipelineGraph (src/haute/_types.py:707-731) computed exactly ONCE per instance and explicitly memoized (its own docstring says 'Cached once per ``PipelineGraph`` instance ... was previously recomputed on every preview cache-key lookup'). Mutating a PipelineGraph in place would NOT recompute the fingerprint; correctness instead relies on the immutable-copy idiom (model_copy clears the memo on the new instance, _types.py:661-671). The two docstrings directly contradict each other, and the _cache.py one asserts the precise opposite of the actual caching strategy — exactly the 'comment describing removed behaviour / misleading invariant claim' class. A reader trusting it could wrongly assume in-place node-config edits are automatically reflected in the cache key.
findings.evidence: _cache.py:194-195 docstring: "Always recomputed to avoid serving stale cached results when the graph instance is mutated (e.g. node config changes)."  Contradicted by _types.py:707 `@cached_property def _haute_base_fingerprint` + :711-718 "Cached once per ``PipelineGraph`` instance ... was previously recomputed on every preview cache-key lookup. Callers evolve a pipeline with ``model_copy(update=...)``; the overridden ``model_copy`` clears the memoised digest."  graph_fingerprint (line 423) uses `base = graph._haute_base_fingerprint` (the cached value), not a fresh `_graph_base_fingerprint(graph)` call.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the _graph_base_fingerprint docstring to match reality: it computes the structural digest, but the result is memoized once per PipelineGraph instance via the `_haute_base_fingerprint` cached_property; freshness across edits is guaranteed by the immutable model_copy idiom (which clears the memo), NOT by recomputation on mutation. Remove the 'Always recomputed ... when the graph instance is mutated' wording, or scope it to 'recomputed per new immutable copy'.

findings.title: parent_demands_for_node comment frames optimiser/ratebook routing as a temporary bridge 'while Slice 3 extracts first-class projection rules' — the extraction it describes as pending has largely already happened
findings.description: The docstring of `parent_demands_for_node` calls itself 'a transitional rule bridge used by the executor while Slice 3 extracts first-class projection rules. Keeping optimiser/ratebook routing here lets future rule extraction happen behind the shared planner facade...'. This frames first-class rule extraction as future work, but the file already contains the extracted, registered first-class rules this comment anticipates: `OptimiserParentDemandRule` (lines 649-727, instantiated as `_OPTIMISER_PARENT_DEMAND_RULE` and registered in `_PROJECTION_RULE_COVERAGE_BY_NODE_TYPE` at line 1714) and `SingleParentPolarsExpressionRule` (lines 1271-1302). `parent_demands_for_node` now merely composes those two already-extracted rules. The 'while Slice 3 extracts / future rule extraction' framing is therefore stale and can mislead a reader into thinking optimiser/ratebook demand is still ad-hoc and unextracted. Low severity/confidence because the function genuinely is still the composition point (the bridge has not been deleted) and the claim does not mislead about runtime correctness.
findings.evidence: Comment (lines 741-744): "This is a transitional rule bridge used by the executor while Slice 3 extracts first-class projection rules. Keeping optimiser/ratebook routing here lets future rule extraction happen behind the shared planner facade without route or executor call-site churn."  Reality: the optimiser rule is already a first-class class (OptimiserParentDemandRule, projection.py:649) and is registered in the node-type coverage registry (projection.py:1711-1715); the single-parent Polars rule is likewise extracted (projection.py:1271). parent_demands_for_node (line 746-755) just ORs the two extracted rules together.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the docstring to describe what the function does today: it composes the already-extracted OptimiserParentDemandRule and SingleParentPolarsExpressionRule into the per-node parent-demand result consumed by compute_prepared_plan. Drop the 'while Slice 3 extracts / future rule extraction' framing, or if a tracking reference is still wanted, restate it as 'remaining composition shim' rather than implying the rules are not yet extracted.
